items.title: Chinese regulators block SoftBank’s $5.4B acquisition of ABB Robotics
items.summary: Chinese regulators have blocked SoftBank's $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB Robotics. This action was due to concerns about the transfer of robotics data overseas for AI model training. China's significant presence in ABB's revenue and local manufacturing further influenced the decision. This event highlights growing geopolitical concerns in the global robotics industry. Furthermore, the text notes related actions by the U.S. government concerning foreign robot imports and technology.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, "Chinese regulators block SoftBank’s $5.4B acquisition of ABB Robotics". This report details the blocking of a proposed $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB Robotics by SoftBank due to concerns regarding the overseas transfer of robotics data for artificial intelligence model training. Chinese regulators cited these data transfer issues and China's established presence in ABB's revenue and local manufacturing as influencing the regulatory decision. The acquisition process was halted following these concerns about data governance and technology transfer protocols within the robotics sector. This event reflects escalating geopolitical tensions affecting the global robotics industry and relates to ongoing actions by the United States government concerning foreign robot imports and technology. This development signals increased scrutiny over cross-border technology flows in the robotics and AI fields.

items.title: Physicl raises $10M to make the digital world real enough for robots
items.summary: Physicl raised $10 million in seed funding to apply its expertise in 3D rendering to improve robot training through more realistic simulations. The company aims to help model designers and robot builders overcome training difficulties by providing realistic synthetic data. Physicl's tool, Studio, allows users to create 3D scenes to generate data for training robots on specific, challenging tasks. The platform seeks to transform unstructured real-world information into high-fidelity physical representations for AI models. This approach allows AI to automatically generate necessary training data, addressing the challenge of manually curating data.
items.audio_script: From TechCrunch - Robotics, Physicl raises ten million dollars in seed funding to make the digital world real enough for robots. The company's tool, Studio, enables users to construct three-dimensional scenes to generate data necessary for training robots on specific and challenging tasks. This platform seeks to convert unstructured real-world information into high-fidelity physical representations for artificial intelligence models, allowing AI to automatically generate requisite training data and circumvent the need for manual data curation. This development signals a shift toward synthetic data generation as a core method for advancing robotic learning and simulation technology.

items.title: Swiss Startup Embodied AI Unveils AIR, a Wheeled Robot Built to Work Beside Factory Staff Without a Cage
items.summary: Embodied AI, a Swiss startup, unveiled AIR, a wheeled robot designed to work alongside factory staff without a safety cage. AIR features a torso with two compliant arms, designed to minimize harm during contact. The robot operates via remote teleoperation during initial training, and it is projected to achieve autonomy within a month. The company reports a 95% task success rate in paid pilots with manufacturers. Embodied AI plans to obtain CE marking in 2027 to comply with EU Machinery Regulation requirements.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, Swiss Startup Embodied AI Unveils AIR, a Wheeled Robot Built to Work Beside Factory Staff Without a Cage. This report details the unveiling of AIR, a wheeled robot designed for collaborative work in factory settings without the need for safety caging, achieving a ninety-five percent task success rate in paid pilot programs with manufacturers. The robot is constructed with a torso and two compliant arms intended to minimize harm upon physical contact with factory personnel. Initial operation is managed through remote teleoperation during the training phase, with the development team projecting full autonomy within a single month. The company is currently planning to secure CE marking in two thousand twenty-seven to align with the European Union Machinery Regulation requirements. This development signals a tangible step toward integrating sophisticated embodied artificial intelligence into complex industrial environments.

items.title: NEURA Robotics Partners With E.ON and enviaM on Grid Robotics, With Trials Expected in 2027
items.summary: NEURA Robotics is partnering with E.ON and enviaM to develop robots for electricity-grid operations, focusing on inspections and asset monitoring. The collaboration will involve training robotic skills using data and simulation at TUM RoboGym. The pilot program, with enviaM's MITNETZ STROM, is expected to begin in 2027. Initial applications will target inspecting equipment and monitoring critical assets in grid facilities.

items.title: Apple's HALO Teaches a Unitree G1 to Navigate Unseen Rooms With Simulation-Generated Data
items.summary: Apple researchers trained a Unitree G1 humanoid using a system called HALO to navigate unseen rooms based on simulation-generated data. HALO successfully completed 91% of 360 single-task trials across six real-world environments without teleoperation. The system uses a multi-layered approach involving a vision-language model, a motion generator, and a motion tracker. Training involved generating 162,698 episodes using synthetic data from 1,000 procedurally generated rooms in Isaac Sim. Although successful in single tasks, chaining skills proved less reliable, highlighting ongoing challenges in real-world generalization.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, "Apple's HALO Teaches a Unitree G1 to Navigate Unseen Rooms With Simulation-Generated Data". The methodology involved a multi-layered approach incorporating a vision-language model, a motion generator, and a motion tracker to facilitate navigation without teleoperation. Training required the generation of one hundred sixty-two thousand six hundred ninety-eight episodes derived from synthetic data within Isaac Sim, generated from one thousand procedurally generated rooms. While the system demonstrated success in completing ninety-one percent of thirty-six zero single-task trials across six real-world environments, chaining skills exhibited reduced reliability, indicating ongoing challenges in real-world generalization. This research points toward continued development in bridging the gap between simulated training and complex physical interaction for robotics.

items.title: How did Agility Robotics perform on its first day on the stock market?
items.summary: Agility Robotics began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker AGLT, claiming to be the first pure-play legged humanoid company to go public. The stock experienced volatility, trading between a low of $8.40 and a high of $12.15, and closed slightly above its opening price at $11.49. Other robotics and technology stocks also experienced declines on the day. Agility Robotics has secured over $300 million in committed orders for its Digit 5 humanoids, with deliveries expected in 2027. The company is also exploring the addition of wheel-based robots to its product lineup.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, "How did Agility Robotics perform on its first day on the stock market?". This segment details the initial trading performance of Agility Robotics upon its public debut. The stock experienced significant volatility, fluctuating between an opening low of eight dollars and forty cents and a high of twelve dollars and fifteen cents, ultimately closing slightly higher at eleven dollars and forty-nine cents. The company, which entered the market under the ticker AGLT as the first pure-play legged humanoid company, secured commitments exceeding three hundred million dollars for its Digit 5 humanoids, with scheduled deliveries projected for two thousand twenty-seven. Furthermore, the company indicated plans to integrate wheel-based robots into its forthcoming product offerings. This debut provides further data points regarding the market reception of specialized robotics technology. Attention remains focused on future delivery schedules and product diversification strategies within the robotics sector.

items.title: How Ambi Robotics helps its customers prepare for peak season
items.summary: Ambi Robotics helps customers prepare for peak season by providing support for increased logistics volume. They assist by offering training and implementing strategies to increase throughput without necessarily installing new systems. Ambi also reduces downtime by forward-deploying spare parts to customer locations. Customer trust is maintained through dedicated personnel for support, training, and maintenance. Furthermore, Ambi uses an internal AI system to assist employees in solving problems and onboarding new staff.

items.title: Xiaomi humanoids complete reported eight hour factory sorting test
items.summary: Two Xiaomi humanoid robots completed an eight-hour parts sorting trial at an electric vehicle factory. The robots successfully retrieved flexible plastic panels from bins and placed them into assembly line racks, demonstrating complex manipulation skills. The robots synchronized with the line's control system and corrected errors during the task. The trial involved variable presentation and flexible parts, unlike simple pick-and-place motions. This test served as a preliminary validation for one workstation, not a full fleet deployment.

items.title: Tokyo Researchers Build Robotic Legs With 3D-Printed Muscles, Tendons and Ligaments
items.summary: Researchers at the University of Tokyo built a life-size robotic leg system using 3D-printed structures mimicking muscles, tendons, and ligaments. They utilized a single flexible TPU material, varying its geometry to achieve different mechanical properties for various body parts. Electric motors pull wires that actuate the legs, while the printed structures provide passive compliance. This method offers a shared design and fabrication process for compliant body parts. The work advances the design and manufacturing of robotic structures, though autonomous walking remains a future challenge.

Autonomous walking remains a future challenge for this technology.

items.title: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.
items.source: MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech
items.summary: A person signed up for a waitlist for a humanoid robot cleaning service in San Francisco, motivated by a desire for a futuristic experience. The robots currently operate with remote human piloting, using collected data to train future autonomous models. The service is expensive compared to the initial offer, and the robots are not yet fully autonomous for complex tasks. The experience revealed that while the robots made some impressive cleaning feats, they struggled with navigation and some tasks required human intervention. The company aims to eventually deploy these robots for various jobs, potentially improving conditions for those in the cleaning industry.

items.title: CMU Introduces Pixel, a Sub-$15,000 Wheeled Robot Designed to Learn From Human Demonstrations
items.summary: Carnegie Mellon University introduced Pixel, a wheeled, two-armed robot with a build cost under $15,000, designed to learn from human demonstrations for coordinated movement. The project focuses on how co-designing the robot's body, controls, and data collection enhances learning. Pixel has demonstrated tasks like tidying and vacuuming, with a companion paper showing 87% average task progress. The system utilizes human-worn tools and sensor data to reconstruct scenes and translate movements, successfully handling complex interactions. The research aims to advance low-cost, accessible mobile manipulation platforms through human instruction.

This development signals a push toward accessible learning methods in robotics and mobile manipulation technology.

items.title: IHMC’s Alex humanoid wins Army xTechHumanoid demonstration stage
items.summary: IHMC's Alex humanoid won the demonstration stage of the U.S. Army's xTechHumanoid competition at Marine Corps Base Quantico. The winning team, along with four others, advanced to structured evaluations with a chance to secure an Army prototype evaluation contract. Alex's success is attributed to hybrid autonomy, integrating AI decision-making with human operator control for complex missions. The competition aimed to assess humanoid capabilities for physically demanding tasks and reducing soldier exposure to danger. Future evaluations will focus on Alex's ability to navigate complex environments, which is a key design challenge.

items.title: Welcome, Amazing Hand!
items.summary: Amazing Hand is an affordable, open-source robotic hand developed by Pollen Robotics. It features a compact design with motors inside the hand, eliminating external cables, and weighs 400 grams. The hand is constructed from 3D printed plastic and flexible shells, utilizing eight Feetech micro servos for its movement. It is positioned as an accessible experimental platform for hobbyists, education, and research rather than a premium dexterous hand. The project is available via ready-made kits or for independent assembly using printed components.

As a prototype, Xiao Di targets markets including car dealerships, education, and industrial uses.

items.title: Ctrl-F: Force as an Interface for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Force is proposed as a natural command channel bridging motion imitation and object interaction for humanoid manipulation. Ctrl-F introduces a hierarchical framework that augments motion tracking with explicit 3-D force commands at designated contact points like hands or feet. This framework allows for the online adjustment of force commands based on object state and proprioception, which is difficult for force-blind trackers. Experimental results show Ctrl-F successfully handles tasks like dragging, pushing, and kicking boxes up to 20kg, adapting to changing loads. Consequently, the system enables effective locomotion manipulation requiring significant, sustained interaction forces.

items.title: MESA: An Evaluation Framework for Compositional, Semantic, and Spatial Generalization in Robotics
items.summary: MESA is an evaluation framework designed to precisely measure language-conditioned policy generalization in robotics. It offers five evaluation suites and four generalization axes: spatial configuration, object instance, object category, and subtask composition. The framework utilizes a pipeline called MESA-Gen for generating tasks and demonstrations at scale. Evaluation on seven baseline methods showed moderate performance, suggesting room for further progress. MESA rankings are broadly consistent with RoboArena scores, indicating relevance beyond simulation.

items.title: ELA: End-to-End Latent Action Policy Learning from Video Demonstrations
items.summary: Robot imitation learning often suffers from limited action-labeled data despite abundant video demonstrations. ELA is an end-to-end framework that learns from video by optimizing latent actions jointly for policy learning and action decoding. It trains a latent action model, policy, and action decoder to leverage video data with few demonstrations. Experiments on manipulation tasks show ELA consistently surpasses previous latent action baselines. The method easily integrates with existing imitation learning approaches using lightweight decoders.

items.title: Contact-Implicit Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization for Dynamic Humanoid Locomotion on Parameterizable Uneven Terrain
items.summary: A trajectory planner is presented for humanoid robots to perform dynamic movements on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. This method generates feasible motions by considering the robot's full dynamics and kinematics without requiring predefined contact sequences. A mathematical model approximates ground geometry with a smooth surface, modeling ground interaction through novel contact constraints for arbitrary surfaces. The approach is validated using nonlinear programming across various terrain topologies, with feasibility tested in simulation and on the ErgoCub robot. Dynamic trajectory generation is achieved by embedding high-level requirements into the optimization cost function.

items.title: $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ Smooth Trajectory Planning with Application to Soft Robots
items.summary: Smooth trajectory planning is crucial for high motion performance and avoiding vibrations in robots, but existing smoothness requirements may be insufficient for soft continuum robots. The work introduces a $\mathcal{C}^\infty$-smooth trajectory generator to address this gap by creating infinitely differentiable paths. These trajectories ensure continuity in velocity, acceleration, jerk, and other derivatives between sequential states. The method specifically handles null boundary conditions where all derivatives at the start and end are zero. The approach was verified through simulations and hardware testing.

items.title: Correct Robots Before They Make Mistakes: Proactive Human-in-the-Loop Intervention via Preference Learning
items.summary: A framework called Proactive Human-in-the-Loop (PHIL) allows operators to intervene by previewing policy predictions before they cause mistakes. During intervention, PHIL uses an extended reality interface to display predicted trajectories and pairs rejected predictions with corrective actions. Preference-based post-training encourages the policy to favor these human corrections. Evaluation on manipulation tasks showed that PHIL increased success rates for diffusion policy and X-VLA compared to other methods. Policies corrected proactively also exhibited fewer unnecessary recovery behaviors in successful episodes.

items.title: OdorSpaces: Visual-Olfactory Embodied Navigation in 3D Environments
items.summary: OdorSpaces is a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation in 3D environments. It augments Habitat-Sim by simulating 3D odor transport and dispersion using the Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS). The system allows agents to navigate photorealistic indoor spaces using both visual and olfactory inputs. Experiments focus on source-seeking tasks like gas-leak and fire localization. A multimodal reinforcement learning policy developed for this system outperforms baselines in visual-olfactory navigation.

items.title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
items.summary: OUCH is a wrist-worn device utilizing pneumatic actuation to deliver controlled, noxious mechanical stimuli for automated neurological assessment. It employs stacked pneumatic pouch actuators, an indenter, and a compliant spacer to ensure the indenter contacts the skin during actuation. Testing demonstrated that OUCH achieved significantly higher localized contact pressure compared to a commercial algometer while eliciting discomfort with less applied force. This work demonstrates a method for objective, uniform, and controlled haptic stimulation. The system provides a foundation for automated neurological assessment in hospitalized patients.

items.title: GRASP: Gradient-Guided Sampling for Contact-Rich Physics-Based Motion Retargeting
items.summary: GRASP proposes a method for physics-based motion retargeting by combining sampling-based exploration with gradient-guided refinement. It extends tempered sequential Monte Carlo by fitting local quadratic cost models to archived rollouts to guide Markov chain Monte Carlo rejuvenation. The approach utilizes gradients from these rollouts to refine the sampling process without needing a differentiable simulator. GRASP-MPC scales this optimization to long demonstrations using warm-started receding-horizon planning. Experiments on hands and humanoids achieved accurate retargeting with minimal task-specific contact rewards.
